passage: I said it in the middle of dinner: "I'll see you all in court." I'm Tushar, and I'm not proud of it. Then I stopped answering calls from my aunt, my cousins, even Manoj, my brother. I thought silence would make them take me seriously. Instead, everyone dug in. Manoj posted a message to the family group listing what he would never give up. Dadi asked to see us both, her voice shaking, and I refused. Months later the house is still shared on paper and empty in every way that matters. There is no talk of settlement now. Every time I imagine one, I can't picture how we would get from here to sitting at one table.

qa.q: What did Tushar say in the middle of dinner?
qa.a: Tushar said, "I'll see you all in court."

qa.q: What does Tushar's remark "I'm not proud of it" suggest about how Tushar feels?
qa.a: It suggests Tushar feels regret and some shame about the threat and the silence that followed.

qa.q: What could Tushar do now to move things forward?
qa.a: Tushar could reach out to Dadi and the family, apologise for the threat, and ask for a calm meeting with a neutral elder.

qa.q: How might Dadi have felt when the brothers refused to meet?
qa.a: Dadi was probably distressed and helpless, as her shaking voice suggests.

grounding: Tushar threatens court and stops speaking to relatives, positions harden, an elder is distressed and settlement seems further away.
